newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-IN-FORM ATLETICO HAVE A POINT TO PROVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-IN-FORM ATLETICO HAVE A POINT TO PROVE.

text.p: Atletico Madrid face up to Saturday's Madrid derby with Real keen to prove wrong those billing it as a clash between last season's champions and their heirs-apparent.

After recovering from a disastrous start that left them 13 points adrift, an Atletico win would take Radomir Antic's side to within five points of Real. And with Barcelona playing away at fourth-placed Betis, the weekend could prove decisive.
If Betis beat Barcelona, a Real victory would leave Fabio Capello's side six points clear at the top. It would also leave Atletico 11 points adrift just before the half-way stage in the championship.

Both Real and Barcelona showed their weakness last weekend by slipping up against the bottom two clubs. However, Real's blushes after their goalless draw at Extremadura were saved the following day by Barcelona's humiliating 3-2 defeat at home by Hercules.

Although Real bounced back on Wednesday with a hard-fought 2-0 Cup win at Valladolid -- with teenager Raul Gonzalez again the star -- former AC Milan coach Capello is aware he is up against a side in form.
Atletico are unbeaten in 10 games and dispatched Zaragoza 5-1 in their last league match. The previous weekend Radomir Antic's side had come home from Extremadura with a 4-2 win.
Victory in the derby game would refloat a championship challenge that was being written off just two months ago.
"It's a very big opportunity. We can cut back three points from one of the direct rivals and enter the leading group with force," Antic said.
However, the Serb may be faced with a crisis in midfield if an appeal against the suspension of Argentine international Diego Simeone is not overturned.
And influential playmaker Jose Luis Caminero, injured while scoring against Zaragoza, is still not on top form.
The possible absences could expose one of the weaknesses of Atletico vis-a-vis their big-spending neighbours.
Whereas Real leave internationals on the bench and several more in the stands every game, Atletico get by on a much thinner squad.

As if to bring home the point, the game should see the debut of Italian defender Christian Panucci, who has moved from AC Milan to rejoin Capello. Another international, Portuguese defender Carlos Secretario, would be relegated to substitute.
Antic and his men are looking for their first victory in nine derby games and are hoping to make it a baptism of fire for the young Italian.
